MODELS AND NODES USED IN THIS WORKFLOW

 Load Diffusion Model

Download pixal3d_int8_convrot.safetensors~5.2 GB 

Place in: ComfyUI/models/diffusion_models/3D

Create the 3D folder if it does not exist.

 Load CLIP Vision

Download dino_v3_L_naf_fp32.safetensors~1.1 GB 

Place in: ComfyUI/models/clip_vision

 Load VAE (two files)

Download trellis_2_shape_vae_bf16.safetensors~1.0 GB 

Download trellis_2_texture_vae_bf16.safetensors~0.9 GB 

Place in: ComfyUI/models/vae

 Remove Background Pixaroma

Download birefnet.safetensors~424 MB 

Place in: ComfyUI/models/background_removal

 Camera Angle Model (MoGe)

Download moge_2_vitl_normal_fp16.safetensors~630 MB 

Place in: ComfyUI/models/geometry_estimation

Pixal3D needs the camera angle of the picture. Trellis 2 does not, so its workflow does not need this file.

 After placing the files, restart ComfyUI or refresh model lists using the R shortcut.

nodes.title: What each node does
widgets_values:
{"version": 1, "content": "

WHAT EACH NODE DOES

The colour of a node tells you what kind of node it is. Nothing here needs changing except the blue ones.

 Models to download

Orange. Each one needs a file from the list in the other note.

  • Load Diffusion Model (Pixal3D) - The model that turns the picture into a 3D shape.
  • Load CLIP Vision (DINOv3) - Reads the picture so the model understands what it is looking at.
  • Load VAE (shape) - Turns the model's output into geometry.
  • Load VAE (texture) - Turns the model's output into colours.
  • Load MoGe Model (camera angle) - Works out the camera angle of your picture. Pixal3D needs it, Trellis 2 does not.
  • Remove Background Pixaroma (cut out) - Cuts the subject away from its background.

 The numbers you set

Blue, and numbered. These are the only nodes you have to touch.

  • 1. Load your image - Your starting picture. One clear object works best.
  • 2. Seed (drives all four samplers) - Same seed, same result. Change it for a different attempt.
  • 3. Texture size (lower = faster) - Size of the baked texture maps.

 Getting the picture ready

Grey. Runs by itself, no numbers to type.

  • Centre and crop to 1024 x 1024 - Puts the subject in the middle at the size the model expects.
  • What the 3D model actually sees - Preview of the cut-out picture. Check it here before a long run.
  • Estimate the scene geometry - Reads depth and normals from the picture.
  • Camera field of view - Turns that depth into a camera angle.
  • Read the picture - Hands the picture to the model as the thing to build.

 Stage 1

Teal. A rough blob, so you can see it is working.

  • Empty 3D latent - The empty space the shape gets built into.
  • Stage 1 - rough voxel blob - First pass. Blocks out roughly where the object is.
  • Decode the blob - Turns that first pass into something viewable.
  • Voxel to Mesh - Converts the blocks into a mesh.
  • Create 3D File (from Mesh) - Writes the mesh out so a viewer can show it.
  • Stage 1 result - the rough blob - What the first pass produced. Lumpy is correct here.

 Stage 2

Purple. The real shape appears.

  • Shape stage - Sets up the pass that finds the real shape.
  • Stage 2 - the real shape - Second pass. The actual form appears.

 Stage 3

Red. The shape is refined and upscaled.

  • Upsample the shape to 1536 (lower to 1024 for more speed) - The biggest speed setting. Lower it if a run takes too long.
  • Stage 3 - refine the shape - Third pass. Cleans up and adds detail.
  • Decode the mesh - Turns the refined result into a mesh.

 Stage 4

Green. The colours are worked out.

  • Texture stage - Sets up the pass that works out the colours.
  • Stage 4 - the colours - Fourth pass. Colour per point on the surface.
  • Decode the colours - Turns that pass into usable colour data.

 After the stages

Amber. Mesh tidy-up, texture baking and saving. All on the processor.

  • Free the VRAM - the rest is mesh work - Hands the graphics memory back. Everything after this runs on the processor.
  • Mesh info (polygon count) - Reports how many points and faces the mesh has.
  • Rebuild the mesh cleanly (768 = denser) - Rebuilds the surface as an even grid of triangles. The model's own mesh is messy in places, and most 3D programs want a tidy one.
  • Reduce to 700k triangles - Cuts the triangle count down to something usable.
  • Smooth the normals - Smooths the shading so the surface does not look faceted.
  • Paint the mesh with the colours - Puts the colours onto the mesh points.
  • Create 3D File (from Mesh) - Writes the mesh out so a viewer can show it.
  • FAST RESULT - vertex colours - Turn it with the mouse. Colour on the points, no texture files.
  • UV unwrap - Flattens the mesh so textures can be painted onto it.
  • Bake colour / roughness / metallic - Renders three texture maps from the coloured mesh.
  • Bake the normal map - Renders a map that fakes small surface detail.
  • Bake ambient occlusion - Renders the soft shadows in the crevices.
  • Base Color - The colour map, for checking.
  • Metallic - The metal map, for checking.
  • Roughness - The roughness map, for checking.
  • Normal - The normal map, for checking.
  • Ambient Occlusion - The shadow map, for checking.
  • Apply all the maps - Attaches every baked map to the mesh.
  • FULL RESULT - saved to output/3d - The finished model with its texture maps, written to output/3d.

 Left alone on purpose

No colour means you never need to change it.

  • Pipeline default - leave alone - Part of how the model runs. Nothing to change.

nodes.title: Settings for your card
widgets_values:
{"version": 1, "content": "

SETTINGS FOR YOUR GRAPHICS CARD

 The four numbers that decide the speed

Everything else in the workflow can stay as it is. Each row says which node to look for.

SettingNode on the canvasLow VRAMHQ24 GB
Upsample resolutionUpsample the shape102415361536
Remesh resolutionRebuild the mesh cleanly5127681024
TrianglesReduce to N triangles200,000700,0001,500,000
Texture size5. Texture size204840964096

The upsample resolution is by far the biggest one, and how much it costs depends on your card. On the 6 GB RTX 2060, dropping it from 1536 to 1024 took one test run from 20 minutes to 2 minutes. On a 24 GB RTX 4090 the same change is much smaller: 39 seconds against 25. Either way there is no difference you can see at normal viewing size, so lower it first if you are short of memory or time, and leave it high if you have the card for it.

Do not go above 1536. The node allows 2048 and it is not worth it: on a 24 GB RTX 4090 the mesh comes back with about five times as many holes in it and the run takes half again as long. Set the 3D view background to a bright colour and you can see them straight through the surface.

 Measured run times

Same picture, same seed, one object.

Workflow6 GB RTX 206024 GB RTX 4090
Trellis 2 - Low VRAM2 min 10 s25 s
Trellis 2 - HQ + PBR Textures40 min2 min 28 s
Pixal3D - Low VRAM6 min 20 s37 s
Pixal3D - HQ + PBR Texturesover 2 hours3 min

Both columns were measured with Kitchen Attention enabled, using the same picture and seed. The first run after starting ComfyUI is a few seconds slower than the table while the models load into the card; run it again for the real speed.

Pixal3D is slower on a small card because it also loads MoGe to work out the camera angle. Trellis 2 does not need it.

 Pixal3D on HQ is not practical on a 6 GB card. It made a much denser mesh than Trellis 2 (15.7 million faces against 11.8 million), and rebuilding a mesh that size runs on a single processor core, so the run was stopped after more than two hours. On a 6 GB card use Pixal3D Low VRAM, or use Trellis 2 for HQ. On a 24 GB card the same run finishes in 3 minutes.

 Why Free VRAM is in the workflow

Memory was sampled every 3 seconds through a full HQ run on the 6 GB test machine. It peaked at 5.47 GB of 6.00 GB, so only 0.53 GB was spare at the worst moment.

The Free VRAM node sits after the last step that needs the graphics card. In the trace it drops memory in use from 5.26 GB straight down to 1.25 GB, right before the mesh and baking work, which is all done on the processor. On a big card it costs nothing.

 If you run out of memory

  • Use the Low VRAM workflow rather than the HQ one.
  • Lower Upsample resolution first, then Texture size.
  • Close other programs using the graphics card, browsers included.
